thread:
ana: Quick thought — can we decouple canary validation from the main ingest path and run runtime assertions in a dedicated canary worker? Trying to avoid blocking model onboarding while still catching regressions early.

sam: +1. Blocking full ingest makes onboarding slow. Proposal: lightweight canary stage that runs a small sample with runtime assertions (latency, shape, kv-cache sanity, basic logits checks).

claire: How do we handle KV cache warmups? Most regressions crop up only after a few prefixes.

rahul: Two-phase warmup: (1) synthetic prefix replay to prime kv, bounded like 200 tokens, (2) one or two real-sample queries to validate correctness. Keeps cost predictable.

ana: Also need golden inputs and predicates — not strict exact-match for sampling models. Use similarity thresholds or rank-stats.

matt: Main worry: kernel/batching path regressions only show up under real batching. Canary worker might miss those if it runs single-shot.

sam: Agreed. Let's do a two-tier canary: lightweight correctness canary during intake + nightly stress canary that replicates production batching and seq-length distributions on dedicated infra.

claire: :thumbsup: For gating, should a failing canary fully block `onboard_ready` or just create a warning?

rahul: Block on critical failures (crashes, shape mismatch, perf regress >30%, severe logit anomalies). Soft-fail (warn) on small latency increases or distributional drifts; escalate.

ana: Recommend assertion DSL attached to model metadata, e.g. `asserts: ["median_lat < 120ms", "output_shape == [1, seq]", "logit_stats.stdev < 0.5"]` — versioned per model.

sam: Those assertions must be editable without re-ingesting the binary. Also persist history in telemetry so we can see regressions over time.

matt: CI integration: any PR touching kernel selection or quantization should run the lightweight canary as part of CI. ci-bot can post the results back.

ci-bot: ci-bot: Canary smoke run queued: `canary-run --model=mdl_123 --mode=light --asserts=meta/asserts.yaml`

ana: Ops playbook: On canary fail -> mark `onboard_status=needs-investigation`, auto-open ticket with logs, traces, golden inputs, and a reproducible `run.sh` snippet.

claire: Cost control: keep light canary tiny; run heavy stress suite nightly on preemptible / cheaper GPUs. We can also stagger stress runs across models by priority.

rahul: For nondeterministic sampling models, switch assertions to distribution checks (token entropy, topk mass, divergence vs baseline) instead of exact logits.

sam: Action items I’ll take: 1) spec canary-worker RPC interface, 2) draft assertion DSL + metadata schema, 3) wire canary result -> onboarding UI, 4) sketch nightly stress schedule and cost estimate.

ana: Thanks. Can we sync tomorrow 11am to review the draft?

sam: Yes, I'll send calendar invite.

matt: Leaving a note — make sure to include KV cache trace and a sample of kernel selection logs in the ticket payload.

ci-bot: ci-bot: Reminder: add `export CANARY_ENV=staging` to the run script for reproducible runs.
